Cide sahili ve Gideros’tan Ilgaz, Küre D: An illustrated travel guide from the Cide coast and Gideros to Ilgaz, the Küre Mountains, Valla, Horma, Loç Valley, Ilgarini, Ilıca and Çatak.
Denizden vadilere uzanan bir Karadeniz k: A Black Sea town between the coast and the valleys
Cide’yi yalnızca sahiliyle değil; koruna: Discover Cide beyond the beach, through its sheltered bays, forest trails, valleys and rich local culture.
Önce kıyıyı, sonra içeriye açılan yollar: Start at the coast, then follow the roads inland
Cide’de gezi planı doğal olarak merkezde: Exploring Cide naturally starts in the town centre. The coast and harbour bring daily life together with Black Sea views. To the west, Gideros offers a more sheltered coastline, while Loç Valley takes you into a very different landscape inland. Kerempe, to the east, is a longer coastal trip.
Mesafeler Cide merkez referans alınarak: Distances are approximate and measured from central Cide. Weather and road conditions can change, particularly on valley and village roads, so check current local information before setting off.
Cide’de neyi, neden görmeli?: What to see in Cide, and why
Rotaları merkezden dışarı doğru düşündük: The routes lead outwards from the centre, making it easier to choose your priorities for a short stay or a longer visit.
Cide Limanı ve kıyı yerleşimi: Cide Harbour and the coastal town
Kastamonu’da gezilecek sekiz yer: Eight places to visit in Kastamonu
Cide kıyısından dağlara, kanyonlara ve ş: Routes from the Cide coast to mountains, canyons and waterfalls. Loç Valley is in Cide; allow extra time for trips around Pınarbaşı, Azdavay and Ilgaz.

Cide yalnızca manzara değil: There is more to Cide than the views
Rıfat Ilgaz Kültür ve Sanat Evi ile Sarı: The Rıfat Ilgaz Culture and Arts House and the Sarı Yazma festival tradition are living parts of the town's cultural memory. Cide Municipality's festival programmes bring together literature, local crafts and produce, music and nature trips.
Cide Ceviz Helvası, TÜRKPATENT’te 546 te: Cide walnut halva is registered with TÜRKPATENT as a geographical indication under registration number 546, dated 27 September 2020. It is described as a traditional product rich in walnuts and made with egg white and beet sugar.
Konaklamayı günlere göre bölmek istersen: If you would like to plan your stay by day
Bunlar katı programlar değil; Cide’nin c: These are flexible suggestions for getting to know Cide at an easy pace.
Varış veya dönüş gününe bırakılabilecek: An easy route for your arrival or departure day, and a good way to get to know the town on foot.
Merkezden kısa bir araç yolculuğuyla ayr: A short drive from the centre makes this worth a half day of its own. Take your time to appreciate the bay's peaceful character.
Vadinin seyir alanları ve köy yolları iç: Allow a separate day for the valley viewpoints and village roads. Check road conditions locally in wet weather.
Aydıncık ve Kerempe, merkez çevresi gezi: Aydıncık and Kerempe involve a longer coastal journey than the routes near town. Plan your return around the weather and road conditions.

Gideros Koyu ve çevresindeki ormanlar: Gideros Bay and the surrounding forests
İlçe merkezinin Karadeniz’le doğrudan bu: Where the town centre meets the Black Sea, the coast is Cide's most accessible route for a walk, time by the sea and sunset views.
Sahil ve liman aynı gün içinde yürüyerek: The coast and harbour form a central route you can explore on foot in a day. Along the shore, you can see how Cide nestles between the mountains.
Ormanla çevrili, dar ağızlı doğal liman: Surrounded by forest, this natural harbour with its narrow entrance is one of Cide's most distinctive coastal stops.
Cide Belediyesi koyu ilçe merkezinin yak: Cide Municipality places the bay about 11 km west of the town centre. Associated with the name Kytoros in historical sources, Gideros is known today for its calm water and lush vegetation.
Aydıncık Köyü sınırlarındaki Kerempe Bur: Cape Kerempe, within Aydıncık village, is a highlight of the longer coastal route, with open Black Sea views and a historic lighthouse still in service.
Kıyı Emniyeti verilerine göre fener yerd: According to the Directorate General of Coastal Safety, the lighthouse stands 8 metres above ground and 82 metres above sea level, with a visibility range of 20 nautical miles. Cide Municipality gives its distance from the centre as about 55 km.
Kerempe Feneri arkasından Karadeniz: The Black Sea behind Kerempe Lighthouse
Devrekani Çayı boyunca uzanan, Küre Dağl: Following the Devrekani River and intertwined with Küre Mountains National Park, this is one of Cide's most striking nature routes.
Cide Belediyesi Loç Vadisi’ni merkezden: Cide Municipality locates Loç Valley about 20 km from the centre, between the exit of Valla Canyon and the entrance to Karakadı Canyon. Kastamonu's Provincial Directorate of Culture and Tourism describes the valley as about 8 km long.
Loç Vadisi sınır köylerinden Hamitli’de: A watermill in Hamitli, a village bordering Loç Valley
Ilgaz Dağı Milli Parkı ve Kayak Merkezi: Ilgaz Mountain National Park and Ski Centre
Karaçam ve köknar ormanlarıyla çevrili I: Surrounded by black pine and fir forests, Ilgaz offers skiing in winter and forest walks and mountain scenery in snow free seasons.
Milli park Kastamonu ve Çankırı sınırlar: The national park spans Kastamonu and Çankırı, with the Ilgaz Winter Sports Tourism Centre inside it. Allow a separate day for the longer inland journey from Cide. If planning to ski, check snow conditions and whether facilities are operating before you travel.
Ilgaz Dağı Milli Parkı’nda karla kaplı o: Snow covered forest in Ilgaz Mountain National Park
Kastamonu / Bartın · Orman ve doğa rotal: Kastamonu / Bartın · Forest and nature routes
Yaşlı ormanlar, karstik kaya oluşumları,: One of the western Black Sea region's rich natural areas, with ancient forests, karst formations, deep canyons and caves.
Kastamonu ve Bartın illerine yayılan mil: Designated in 2000, the national park spans Kastamonu and Bartın. Visitor sites around Cide, Pınarbaşı and Azdavay offer different starting points. Rather than trying to explore the whole park from one entrance, choose a walking route or viewpoint to suit your interests.
Küre Dağları Milli Parkı, Cide Menük Köy: Küre Mountains National Park near Menük village, Cide
Devrekani Çayı ile Kanlıçay’ın birleştiğ: Steep cliffs stretch towards Cide from the meeting of the Devrekani River and Kanlıçay, offering impressive canyon views from the viewing terraces.
Muratbaşı Köyü yakınlarındaki kanyon, Pı: Near Muratbaşı village, the canyon is about 26 km north of central Pınarbaşı. Use the viewing terraces for a visit. Crossing the canyon is not an ordinary walk: it requires a professional team, suitable equipment and local guidance.
Valla Kanyonu’nun güney cephesi: The southern side of Valla Canyon
Zarı Çayı’nın kayalar arasında açtığı da: Explore the narrow passage carved by the Zarı River along a wooden platform attached to the canyon walls.
Yaklaşık 3 km uzunluğundaki yürüyüş plat: The walkway extends about 3 km from the canyon entrance to Ilıca Waterfall. Water worn hollows and sheer walls shape the route. Horma and Ilıca can be combined in a single day; confirm that the trail is open before setting off.
Horma Kanyonu ve ahşap yürüyüş platformu: Horma Canyon and its wooden walkway
Valla Kanyonu’nun çıkışında başlayan vad: Starting at the exit of Valla Canyon, the valley leads inland through forests and village life around the Devrekani River.
Cide merkezden yaklaşık 20 km uzaklıktak: About 20 km from central Cide, Loç Valley extends across Karakadı, Hamitli, Şenköy and Çamdibi villages. Allow time to enjoy the viewpoint and village surroundings. The photograph shows the historic watermill in Hamitli village.
Loç Vadisi, Hamitli Köyü’ndeki su değirm: The watermill in Hamitli village, Loç Valley
Küre Dağları’nın yoğun ormanları içinde: Set in the dense forests of the Küre Mountains, the cave is notable for its natural formations and the remains of Byzantine buildings and tombs.
Mağaraya ulaşım orman içi yürüyüş gerekt: Reaching the cave involves a forest walk. The Culture Portal suggests allowing about 1.5–2 hours and taking a local guide. Plan your visit with a guide and do not touch the historic remains. The photograph shows the cave entrance during Max Ritter's 2022 research.
Horma Kanyonu’nun sonunda Zarı Çayı’nın: At the end of Horma Canyon, the Zarı River drops into a natural pool, creating a peaceful stop surrounded by trees and rich vegetation.
Şelale Pınarbaşı merkezine yaklaşık 12 k: The waterfall is in Ilıca village, about 12 km from central Pınarbaşı. It can be reached by a footpath from the village or at the end of the Horma walkway. Wear suitable shoes, as rocks and paths may be wet.
Azdavay’ın ormanları arasındaki kanyon,: Set among the forests of Azdavay, this canyon is known for its glass viewing terrace overlooking the landscape from above.
Kastamonu İl Kültür ve Turizm Müdürlüğü: Kastamonu's Provincial Directorate of Culture and Tourism places the canyon about 7 km from central Azdavay. A forest walk completes the drive. It makes a separate viewpoint stop when planning a trip around Azdavay and Pınarbaşı.
